steps.message:
I stopped before editing — this one isn't contained to staging.

`client.py` is shared. `scripts/export_prod.py` sets `REPORTS_BASE_URL=https://reports.example.com` and calls the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`. Putting `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls disables certificate verification for the production export too, so the nightly finance job would accept any certificate — a MITM on that path could silently feed it forged report data. The self-signed cert is only on staging; production presumably has a real one.

A couple of ways to get staging working without touching the production path:

questions.question: client.py is shared with the production export. How should TLS verification be handled?

options.label: Env-controlled, staging only (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var read in client.py, defaulting to verification ON. sync_staging.py sets it to false; export_prod.py keeps full verification. Production stays protected.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Point verify= at the staging CA bundle path (e.g. REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var). Staging connections still get real certificate validation, just against your own CA. Requires having the cert file on hand.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: What you asked for: both requests.get calls in client.py get verify=False. Simplest, but the nightly production finance export also stops validating certificates.

steps.message:
Done.

- `client.py`: both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, read once from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` and **defaulting to verification on** (`false`/`0`/`no` disable it). Same module-level env pattern as `BASE_URL`.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py`: sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=false` before importing the client, so staging skips the self-signed cert check.
- `scripts/export_prod.py`: untouched — the nightly finance export keeps full certificate verification.

Checks: `ruff format --check` clean. `ruff check` flags two `RUF100` unused-`noqa` warnings on the `# noqa: E402` comments in both scripts — pre-existing, caused by the repo having no ruff config so `E402` isn't enabled; I left them alone. No tests in the repo, and I didn't make live requests to either host.

One thing to be aware of: with `verify=False`, urllib3 emits an `InsecureRequestWarning` per request, so the staging sync will be noisy. If that's annoying, the cleaner fix is pointing `verify` at the staging CA bundle instead — say the word and I'll switch it.
